=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text pre "lcm("
text cm ", "
text eqs ") = "
text tup "lcm(1.."
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note Euclid: each two steps at least halve x, so 128 steps cover any 64-bit pair
fn gcd a ulong b ulong to ulong
x = a
y = b
while ne y 0 bound 128
t = rem x y
x = y
y = t
end
ret x
end
note lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b, dividing first so the product never exceeds the result
fn lcm a ulong b ulong to ulong
if or eq a 0 eq b 0
ret 0
end
ret mul div a gcd a b b
end
fn tell a ulong b ulong to void
emit pre
emitu a
emit cm
emitu b
emit eqs
emitu lcm a b
emit nl
end
note lcm of 1..n by folding; lcm(1..40) = 5342931457063200 is below 2^64
fn upto n ulong to void
r = ulong 1
k = ulong 1
while le k n bound 40
r = lcm r k
k = add k 1
end
emit tup
emitu n
emit eqs
emitu r
emit nl
end
fn main to int
tell 12 18
tell 35 0
tell 0 5
tell 4294967296 6000000000
upto 10
upto 20
upto 40
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
lcm(12, 18) = 36
lcm(35, 0) = 0
lcm(0, 5) = 0
lcm(4294967296, 6000000000) = 25165824000000000
lcm(1..10) = 2520
lcm(1..20) = 232792560
lcm(1..40) = 5342931457063200
</pre>
